## Observed (pm 2026.10.19)

#1481 added the sort key to the brief projection when `--sort <field>` is given. The **default** sort has the same gap, and it is the path agents hit most often (`pm list --status open`, the deprecated `pm list-open`, the AGENTS.md quickstart):

```console
$ pm list --status open --limit 3
items[3]{id,status,type,title}:
  pm-cli-website-e8fs,open,Decision,pm is context management for any agent …
  pm-cli-website-xuvj,open,Task,Roll out canonical hoisted merge-driver guard …
  pm-cli-website-nodo,open,Issue,Fleet release provenance can name the workflow trigger …
sorting:
  sort: "default"
  order: "asc"

$ pm list --status open --limit 8 --fields id,priority,updated_at
  pm-cli-website-e8fs,0,"2026-10-18T06:59:09.673Z"
  pm-cli-website-xuvj,0,"2026-09-26T17:29:15.963Z"
  …
  pm-cli-website-4d5h,1,"2026-10-19T12:25:28.219Z"
```

The default order is priority ascending, then `updated_at` descending. Neither key is in the brief rows, and `sorting.sort: "default"` does not say what "default" means. An agent that reads `.priority` from `--json` gets nothing for every row. In this session an orientation script printed `None` as the priority of all 107 open items and sorted them by an absent key. The agent then needed a second call with `--fields` to recover the ranking the first call had already applied.

## Proposal

- Resolve `sort: "default"` to its real keys in the envelope, for example `sorting: {sort: "priority,updated_at", order: "asc,desc", default: true}`, so the ordering explains itself.
- Under `--brief` (the default list projection), add `priority` as one extra column when the effective sort includes it, exactly as #1481 does for an explicit `--sort`. In TOON that is a single digit per row. Record it in `projection.fields` so the omission receipt stays accurate. `updated_at` can stay behind the receipt, since it is a tiebreak.
- An explicit `--fields` stays authoritative, as in #1481.

Token cost: about 2 bytes per row. It saves the second `--fields` round trip that every triage pass makes today.
GH-1507: Explain effective default list ordering in brief rows and metadata

Verified on current source: pm list --status open --limit3 --json returns only id status type title, projection.fields matches those four, and sorting reports default/asc. GitHub1507 asks for the actual default ordering keys and visible priority without requiring a second --fields read. Keep the completed explicit-sort fix pm-gh1481 closed and preserve the compact default TOON projection from pm-6pycus. Implement the effective sort contract in the SDK for CLI MCP and extensions with additive compatible envelope metadata.

Default sort metadata exposes its effective keys and directions without breaking existing sorting consumers; Brief projection includes priority when the effective sort uses it and updates projection.fields and omission receipts accurately; Explicit --fields compact and full selections remain authoritative and explicit-sort behavior stays covered; Public SDK CLI MCP and TOON/JSON use the same effective sort policy with configured defaults and stable tie breaking; Focused and packed regression controls reproduce the current default path and preserve bounded row/token continuation
Agents can understand default list ranking from one bounded read, while explicit field selection and existing sorting/continuation compatibility remain intact.

## Observed (pm 2026.10.19)

#1481 added the sort key to the brief projection when `--sort <field>` is given. The **default** sort has the same gap, and it is the path agents hit most often (`pm list --status open`, the deprecated `pm list-open`, the AGENTS.md quickstart):

```console
$ pm list --status open --limit 3
items[3]{id,status,type,title}:
  pm-cli-website-e8fs,open,Decision,pm is context management for any agent …
  pm-cli-website-xuvj,open,Task,Roll out canonical hoisted merge-driver guard …
  pm-cli-website-nodo,open,Issue,Fleet release provenance can name the workflow trigger …
sorting:
  sort: "default"
  order: "asc"

$ pm list --status open --limit 8 --fields id,priority,updated_at
  pm-cli-website-e8fs,0,"2026-10-18T06:59:09.673Z"
  pm-cli-website-xuvj,0,"2026-09-26T17:29:15.963Z"
  …
  pm-cli-website-4d5h,1,"2026-10-19T12:25:28.219Z"
```

The full default comparator groups nonterminal items before terminal items, then sorts by priority ascending, `updated_at` descending, and finally ID ascending (using the existing ID comparator). A status-filtered open list hides the terminal grouping but does not remove it from the unfiltered default contract. Neither key is in the brief rows, and `sorting.sort: "default"` does not say what "default" means. An agent that reads `.priority` from `--json` gets nothing for every row. In this session an orientation script printed `None` as the priority of all 107 open items and sorted them by an absent key. The agent then needed a second call with `--fields` to recover the ranking the first call had already applied.

## Proposal

- Preserve the compatible legacy `sorting.sort: "default"` / `order: "asc"` fields and add ordered effective-key metadata covering every comparator stage: terminal-status grouping (`nonterminal_before_terminal`, derived from the active status registry), `priority` ascending, `updated_at` descending, and `id` ascending. An unfiltered list must disclose all four entries in that order; the synthetic terminal-status key must explicitly describe its grouping semantics instead of pretending to be an ordinary stored field. The final field names are a design choice, while completeness and ordering are contract requirements.
- Under `--brief` (the default list projection), add `priority` as one extra column when the effective sort includes it, exactly as #1481 does for an explicit `--sort`. In TOON that is a single digit per row. Record it in `projection.fields` so the omission receipt stays accurate. `updated_at` can stay behind the receipt, since it is a tiebreak.
- An explicit `--fields` stays authoritative, as in #1481.

Token cost: about 2 bytes per row. It saves the second `--fields` round trip that every triage pass makes today.

Default-sort metadata preserves compatible legacy sort/order fields and exposes an ordered effective-key contract including registry-derived nonterminal-before-terminal grouping, priority ascending, updated_at descending and final ID ascending; Unfiltered lists disclose every comparator stage and the synthetic terminal grouping semantics explicitly; Brief projection includes priority when the effective sort uses it and updates projection.fields and omission receipts accurately; Explicit fields compact and full selections remain authoritative and explicit-sort behavior stays covered; Public SDK CLI MCP and TOON/JSON share the effective policy with configured defaults and stable tie breaking; Focused and packed controls preserve bounded continuation
